sentences.en: Not too long ago, anxiety disorders were considered by many to be a personal weakness rather than a true illness, especially in children.
sentences.zh: 不久前，焦虑症在许多人眼中还被认为是一种个人性格缺陷，而不是一种真正的疾病，在儿童群体中尤其如此。

sentences.en: Thankfully, this stigma is on the decline, but finding appropriate treatments for children isn't always easy.
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地，这种污名化正在减少，但为儿童找到合适的治疗方法并不总是那么容易。

sentences.en: In this episode, we speak with a psychologist who has been researching the best treatments and assessments for anxiety disorders.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们邀请到了一位长期研究焦虑症最佳治疗方法和评估手段的心理学家。

sentences.en: She tells us what parents, teachers, and anyone who works with kids needs to know.
sentences.zh: 她将为我们讲述家长、老师以及所有与孩子们共事的人所需要了解的知识。

sentences.en: I'm Audrey Hamilton, and this is Speaking Up Psychology.
sentences.zh: 我是奥黛丽·汉密尔顿，这里是《直面心理学》。

sentences.en: Psychologist Golda Ginsberg is a professor of psychiatry at the University of Connecticut Health Center and has been developing treatments for anxious youth for more than 20 years.
sentences.zh: 心理学家戈尔达·金斯伯格是康涅狄格大学健康中心的精神病学教授，20多年来一直致力于为焦虑的青少年开发治疗方法。

sentences.en: She led the largest national longitudinal study of anxious youth in the United States to examine the long-term outcomes of anxiety treatments
sentences.zh: 她曾领导了美国规模最大的青少年焦虑全国纵向研究，旨在考察焦虑治疗的长期效果，

sentences.en: and is now following up with a study to examine the long-term effect of family-based treatments for the children of anxious parents.
sentences.zh: 目前她正在跟进一项研究，以考察针对焦虑父母的子女开展以家庭为基础的治疗的长期效果。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Ginsberg.
sentences.zh: 欢迎您，金斯伯格博士。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 您好。

sentences.en: Nice to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: I want to start by talking about what an anxiety disorder is.
sentences.zh: 我想从什么是焦虑症开始谈起。

sentences.en: How is it defined?
sentences.zh: 它是如何定义的？

sentences.en: I think a lot of people worry when their child is anxious in certain situations, such as starting in a new school, for example.
sentences.zh: 我想很多人在孩子在特定情况下表现出焦虑时都会感到担心，比如刚上新学校的时候。

sentences.en: But it might be helpful for them to understand the difference between everyday anxiety and anxiety that is a problem in need of professional help.
sentences.zh: 但让他们了解日常焦虑与需要专业帮助的问题性焦虑之间的区别，可能会有所帮助。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that?
sentences.zh: 您能谈谈这一点吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: It's a great question and one that I hear from parents all the time.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极好的问题，也是家长们经常向我提出的问题。

sentences.en: Because anxiety is an emotion that we all experience.
sentences.zh: 因为焦虑是我们所有人都会体验到的一种情绪。

sentences.en: And in fact, anxiety can be quite helpful to us.
sentences.zh: 事实上，焦虑对我们相当有益。

sentences.en: It protects us from dangerous situations.
sentences.zh: 它能保护我们免受危险环境的伤害。

sentences.en: In the school context, it helps us to study when we have a test coming up.
sentences.zh: 在学校的语境下，当我们要考试时，它能帮助我们学习。

sentences.en: So anxiety is something we want to make friends with in a way.
sentences.zh: 所以，从某种程度上说，焦虑是我们想要与之交朋友的东西。

sentences.en: But there does come a time when anxiety becomes problematic.
sentences.zh: 但焦虑确实也会在某个时刻演变成问题。

sentences.en: The definition, just to go back to your first question, the definition of what an anxiety disorder is, for anyone who wants to look at it,
sentences.zh: 回到你的第一个问题，关于焦虑症的定义，对于任何想要了解它的人来说，

sentences.en: is in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual that's published by the American Psychiatric Association.
sentences.zh: 它都写在由美国精神医学学会出版的《诊断与统计手册》中。

sentences.en: And it's essentially a list of symptoms that occur and also impair the functioning of children.
sentences.zh: 它本质上是一系列出现并会损害儿童功能的症状列表话。

sentences.en: So that said, there isn't a blood test that you can get to know whether your child or even an adult has an anxiety disorder.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，并没有哪种血液检测能让你知道你的孩子甚至成年人是否患有焦虑症。

sentences.en: So we look to these symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要看这些症状。

sentences.en: And again, as I said, because anxiety is something we all experience,
sentences.zh: 而且正如我刚才所说，因为焦虑是我们所有人都会体验到的，

sentences.en: we can look to what I think are three key symptoms to identify the signs.
sentences.zh: 我们可以通过我认为是三个关键症状来识别这些迹象。

sentences.en: The first set of symptoms are physiological symptoms, so somatic complaints.
sentences.zh: 第一组症状是生理症状，也就是躯体不适的主诉。

sentences.en: What we know is that children, and adults too, who struggle with anxiety, report headaches and stomach aches where there's no medical cause.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，受焦虑困扰的儿童（成年人也是如此）经常会报告头痛和胃痛，但却找不到医学上的原因。

sentences.en: So that's one sign that parents can look for as they're trying to sort out, is this anxiety that's problematic or not?
sentences.zh: 因此，这是家长在试图弄清楚这究竟是有问题的焦虑还是正常现象时，可以寻找的一个迹象。

sentences.en: The second is that we see these children engage in ways of thinking that if we can get them to articulate what their thoughts are, the themes are full of fear and danger.
sentences.zh: 第二点是，我们发现这些儿童的思维方式表现为——如果我们能让他们表达出他们的想法，其主题往往充满了恐惧和危险。

sentences.en: All the kids are going to laugh at me.
sentences.zh: 所有的孩子都会嘲笑我。

sentences.en: I'm going to fail my teSt.
sentences.zh: 我考试要不及格了。

sentences.en: What if my mom or dad dies?
sentences.zh: 如果我爸爸妈妈死了怎么办？

sentences.en: So those kinds of thoughts are what we notice.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们注意到的是这类想法。

sentences.en: And again, another sign that the child's struggling with anxiety.
sentences.zh: 这也是孩子正遭受焦虑困扰的另一个迹象。

sentences.en: The third is in their behavior.
sentences.zh: 第三点体现在他们的行为上。

sentences.en: And the most common and most problematic behavior is avoidance.
sentences.zh: 最常见也是最具问题性的行为就是回避。

sentences.en: So as children struggle with anxiety, they begin to avoid what they're afraid of.
sentences.zh: 当儿童与焦虑抗争时，他们会开始回避令他们恐惧的事物。

sentences.en: So if they're afraid of taking tests, they'll avoid going to school.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果他们害怕考试，就会逃学。

sentences.en: If they're afraid of something terrible happening to their parents, they'll avoid being away from their parents.
sentences.zh: 如果他们害怕父母发生什么可怕的意外，就会避免离开父母。

sentences.en: They'll sleep with them.
sentences.zh: 他们会和父母睡在一起。

sentences.en: So avoidance is a big behavior to look for.
sentences.zh: 因此，回避是需要重点关注的一种行为。

sentences.en: So those are the three signs that parents can pay attention to.
sentences.zh: 这就是家长可以注意的三个迹象。

sentences.en: That said, we might all, if we're, say, afraid of flying, we might worry the plane's going to crash, or we might start to feel butterflies in our stomach as we're going.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，如果我们比如害怕坐飞机，我们可能会担心飞机坠毁，或者我们在登机时会感到胃里七上八下。

sentences.en: But it doesn't really impair our functioning.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有真正损害我们的功能。

sentences.en: We take the plane anyway.
sentences.zh: 我们还是会坐飞机。

sentences.en: So when we start to see children's lives being impaired by these symptoms, that's when it begins to cross over that line to being helpful and adaptive to being harmful
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们开始看到儿童的生活因这些症状而受损时，这就开始跨越界限，从有益和适应性的状态转变为有害的、

sentences.en: and something that warrants further evaluation and perhaps treatment.
sentences.zh: 需要进一步评估甚至治疗的问题。

sentences.en: Now, anxiety symptoms aren't always the same in all children, correct?
sentences.zh: 那么，焦虑症状在所有儿童身上并不总是相同的，对吗？

sentences.en: For example, you know, what do we know about how anxiety manifests itself in girls versus boys?
sentences.zh: 例如，你知道的，我们对女孩和男孩身上焦虑表现的差异了解多少？

sentences.en: You know, what accounts for those differences?
sentences.zh: 是什么导致了这些差异？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there are, so if you go to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual, there are several kinds of anxiety disorders, if you will.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你去翻阅《诊断与统计手册》，里面有几种不同的焦虑症。

sentences.en: And really, the differences have to do with what the children are afraid of.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这些差异与孩子们害怕的内容有关。

sentences.en: And we do see some patterns across development.
sentences.zh: 并且我们确实在成长过程中看到了一些规律。

sentences.en: So younger children will more likely be afraid of separation from their parents, whereas older adolescents or older children and into adolescence will have more social anxiety.
sentences.zh: 因此，年龄较小的儿童更可能害怕与父母分离，而较大的儿童或进入青春期的青少年则会有更多的社交焦虑。

sentences.en: And in some ways, this could be a reflection of typical developmental fears that go awry.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这可能是步入歧途的典型发展期恐惧的反映。

sentences.en: So as teenagers develop a consciousness about what their peers think about them, typical,
sentences.zh: 随着青少年开始意识到同龄人对他们的看法，典型的、

sentences.en: physical, a child struggling with anxiety, will blow those fears out of proportion to the situation.
sentences.zh: 生理上的、受焦虑困扰的孩子，会把这些恐惧无限放大，脱离实际情况。

sentences.en: And then that anxiety begins to impair their functioning.
sentences.zh: 然后这种焦虑就开始损害他们的功能。

sentences.en: When we look at girls versus boys, we don't, once a child has an anxiety disorder, we don't see many differences between boys and girls.
sentences.zh: 当我们比较女孩和男孩时，一旦孩子患上了焦虑症，我们在男孩和女孩之间并没有看到太多差异。

sentences.en: Prior, what we call subclinical, we see more girls expressing fears in general than boys.
sentences.zh: 在之前我们称之为亚临床的阶段，我们看到女孩普遍比男孩表达出更多的恐惧。

sentences.en: Not sure we know the reasons.
sentences.zh: 我们不太确定其中的原因。

sentences.en: Some suggest it's hormonal or biological.
sentences.zh: 有人认为这与荷尔蒙或生物学因素有关。

sentences.en: Some suggest that it's social in the way that girls are raised.
sentences.zh: 也有人认为是女孩被抚养长大过程中的社会因素造成的。

sentences.en: Kind of when we look at the relation between femininity, for instance, and anxiety, we know there's a positive or correlation.
sentences.zh: 比如，当我们观察女性气质与焦虑之间的关系时，我们知道它们之间存在正相关关系。

sentences.en: So it's probably a combination of the two.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是两者的结合。

sentences.en: Now, your research focuses on anxiety treatments.
sentences.zh: 现在，你的研究重点是焦虑症的治疗。

sentences.en: Now, as a parent, I imagine it's very difficult to decide what the appropriate treatment for my own child is, but your research suggests there are some best practices overall,
sentences.zh: 作为一名家长，我能想象要决定对自己的孩子采取什么适当的治疗是非常困难的，但你的研究表明，总体上存在一些最佳实践，

sentences.en: using evidence-based treatments such as cognitive behavioral therapy and medications.
sentences.zh: 即使用基于证据的治疗方法，如认知行为疗法和药物治疗。

sentences.en: What has your research found on that?
sentences.zh: 你的研究对此有什么发现？

sentences.en: We conducted the largest, what's called a comparative clinical trial.
sentences.zh: 我们开展了规模最大的所谓比较临床试验。

sentences.en: So comparing different treatments to see which one is the beSt.
sentences.zh: 也就是比较不同的治疗方法，看看哪一种最好。

sentences.en: And in the largest trial that we did, which is 488 children were involved and adolescents were involved in the study,
sentences.zh: 在我们开展的规模最大的试验中，有488名儿童和青少年参与了这项研究，

sentences.en: we compared sertraline, which is an SSRI, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, to cognitive behavioral therapy.
sentences.zh: 我们将舍曲林（这是一种SSRI，即选择性5-羟色胺再摄取抑制剂）与认知行为疗法进行了比较。

sentences.en: That's a medication.
sentences.zh: 那是一种药物。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: To cognitive behavioral therapy, which is a talk therapy, which teaches children specific skills to how to manage and reduce their anxiety,
sentences.zh: 与认知行为疗法进行对比，这是一种谈话疗法，它教导儿童如何管理和减轻焦虑的具体技巧，

sentences.en: in which exposure or facing your fear is a key component of that treatment, and the combination of the two to a pill placebo, so a fake inert pill.
sentences.zh: 其中暴露疗法或直面恐惧是该疗法的核心组成部分，此外还将两者的结合与安慰剂（即虚假无害的药丸）进行了对比。

sentences.en: And what we found after 12 weeks was that the children who received the combination treatment did the beSt.
sentences.zh: 我们在12周后发现，接受联合治疗的儿童效果最好。

sentences.en: So about 80% of those children were what we call responders, meaning that they showed clinically meaningful improvement in their anxiety symptoms and in their functioning.
sentences.zh: 因此，大约80%的这些儿童成为了所谓的“有反应者”，这意味着他们的焦虑症状和功能都显示出了临床上有意义的改善。

sentences.en: Both cognitive behavioral therapy and the medicine alone were more effective than the inert pill, but there was no difference between the two of those monotherapies.
sentences.zh: 认知行为疗法和单纯药物治疗都比安慰剂更有效，但这两种单一疗法之间没有差异。

sentences.en: So one wasn't better than the other?
sentences.zh: 所以没有哪一种比另一种更好吗？

sentences.en: One was not better than the other.
sentences.zh: 确实没有哪一种比另一种更好。

sentences.en: So as a parent struggles with what treatment is best for their child, they have choices.
sentences.zh: 因此，当家长在纠结哪种治疗对孩子最好时，他们是有选择的。

sentences.en: And depending on their own preferences and their child's and the severity of their child's anxiety, they might pick one of those three.
sentences.zh: 根据他们自己的偏好、孩子的偏好以及孩子焦虑的严重程度，他们可能会选择这三者之一。

sentences.en: I know for some parents, giving medication is something they're reluctant to do to their child.
sentences.zh: 我知道对某些家长来说，给孩子服药是他们不太愿意做的事情。

sentences.en: But what I'm curious, I think a lot of the issue is they wonder, is my child going to be on this medication forever?
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇，我认为很多问题在于他们在想，我的孩子会一辈子吃这种药吗？

sentences.en: You know, is an anxiety disorder typically a long-term problem?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，焦虑症通常是一个长期问题吗？

sentences.en: Can someone grow out of it, for example?
sentences.zh: 比如，有人能随着年龄增长自然康复吗？

sentences.en: Or will they always need to monitor it and seek treatment?
sentences.zh: 还是说他们需要一直监测并寻求治疗？

sentences.en: So if medication is part of the treatment, you know, is it riskier to give drugs to children than to adults?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果药物治疗是治疗的一部分，给儿童用药会比给成年人用药风险更高吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, terrific questions.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常棒的问题。

sentences.en: And I'm not sure we have all the answers.
sentences.zh: 我不敢说我们已经有了所有的答案。

sentences.en: So let me start with, is it risky?
sentences.zh: 那么让我从“它是否有风险”开始说起。

sentences.en: We have no long-term data on the impact or negative consequences of medication for anxiety.
sentences.zh: 我们目前还没有关于焦虑症药物治疗影响或负面后果的长期数据。

sentences.en: We just don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们只是不知道。

sentences.en: We are completing a study right now looking at this.
sentences.zh: 我们现在正在完成一项研究来探讨这个问题。

sentences.en: And I know my colleagues at other universities are doing the same thing because it's data that's essential.
sentences.zh: 我知道我在其他大学的同事也在做同样的事情，因为这是至关重要的数据。

sentences.en: We don't have it yet.
sentences.zh: 我们目前还没有。

sentences.en: That said, the study that we're completing right now, which actually follows children up to 9 to 10 years after they were initially enrolled in a treatment study for anxiety,
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我们正在完成的这项研究实际上追踪了儿童在最初参加焦虑治疗研究9到10年后的情况，

sentences.en: suggests that a good proportion of these children continue to struggle with anxiety.
sentences.zh: 结果表明，相当一部分儿童仍在与焦虑作斗争。

sentences.en: 30% are chronically ill over time, and we need better treatments for that group.
sentences.zh: 30%的人随着时间推移患有慢性疾病，我们需要针对这一群体提供更好的治疗方法。

sentences.en: About half of them, half of these children, are relapsing.
sentences.zh: 大约有一半的儿童会复发。

sentences.en: So they get better, but then they get worse, and then they get better, and then they get worse.
sentences.zh: 所以他们好了，但然后又恶化了，接着又好了，然后又恶化了。

sentences.en: So we need better ways to monitor and understand why they might get worse over time, but then rebound.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们需要更好的方法来监测和理解为什么他们的病情随着时间推移会恶化，但随后又会反弹。

sentences.en: And then about 20% to 25% get well and stay well.
sentences.zh: 大约20%到25%的人痊愈了并且保持健康。

sentences.en: So I think the bottom line is it is a chronic illness.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得底线是，它是一种慢性病。

sentences.en: It is also possible that a good proportion get better and stay better, but that we need a better system of monitoring.
sentences.zh: 同样也有可能相当一部分人好转后能一直保持健康，但我们需要一个更好的监测系统。

sentences.en: And like we do in dentistry, for instance, we have annual checkups, or my insurance plan lets me go every six months.
sentences.zh: 就像我们在牙科所做的那样，我们有年度体检，或者我的保险计划允许我每六个月去一次。

sentences.en: So I think we need to think about mental health using a different model, something akin to what we do for other illnesses,
sentences.zh: 因此我认为我们需要用一种不同的模式来思考心理健康，这类似于我们为其他疾病所做的事情，

sentences.en: well, baby checks or dentistry, so that we can catch children prior to them relapsing.
sentences.zh: 比如婴儿保健或牙科检查，这样我们就能在儿童复发之前捕捉到迹象。

sentences.en: Now, anxiety is the most common psychiatric disorder among young people, even more than ADHD and depression.
sentences.zh: 焦虑是年轻人中最常见的精神障碍，甚至超过了多动症和抑郁症。

sentences.en: Do we know why it's so common?
sentences.zh: 我们知道它为什么这么常见吗？

sentences.en: Is it more prevalent in more recent generations, if so?
sentences.zh: 它在最近几代人中是否更普遍了？如果是的话，

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: I'm not sure why it's so common.
sentences.zh: 我不太确定它为什么这么普遍。

sentences.en: I think there's certainly a lot to worry about today.
sentences.zh: 我认为现在确实有很多令人担忧的事情。

sentences.en: But I think there are some studies that show it is more prevalent today.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为有一些研究表明它在今天更为普遍。

sentences.en: It's hard to tease apart whether that's because of the methods and the tools we have to identify children are better,
sentences.zh: 这很难厘清，究竟是因为我们用来识别儿童的方法和工具更先进了，

sentences.en: and so we're just doing a better job, or whether actually the prevalence has been increasing over time.
sentences.zh: 所以我们做得更好了，还是说患病率本身确实随着时间推移在增加。

sentences.en: I think it's hard to know.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很难知道。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Ginsburg, thank you so much for joining us.
sentences.zh: 金斯伯格博士，非常感谢您做客我们的节目。

sentences.en: It's been a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 非常荣幸。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢您。
